annotations.title: Check one action against a mandate

description:
Check ONE proposed action against a signed agent mandate BEFORE it happens. Returns {"verdict": "ALLOW"|"DENY", "rule": <name>} plus a report with a ledger fingerprint.

Six rules run in a fixed order, so a refusal names the most important reason rather than an incidental one: amount, payee, audience, currency, window, intent. Anything unclassified is DENY.

Use immediately before any action that spends money, moves a credential or changes state on someone else's behalf.

Do NOT use to: verify mandate signatures (AP2 does that, and this server runs after signature verification), execute the action (it only decides), or certify that an intent is truthful — "intent" arrives from the agent and is untrusted input. An agent that lies within its limits still leaves a ledger entry; proving what really happened is attest's job, not this one's.

Amounts are integer minor units (cents), never floats. Window bounds are inclusive. Fully idempotent: the same inputs always give the same verdict and the mandate is never mutated.

amount_minor.description: Amount in minor units, same scale as max_amount_minor.

at.description: When the action would happen, unix seconds.

audience.description: Audience the payment would go to.

intent.description: What the agent says it is doing. Untrusted.

payee_id.description: Payee the agent is about to use.

mandate.description: The signed authority being enforced. Treat as read-only input.

allowed_intents.description: Permitted intents. Empty means any intent is allowed.

audience.description: Merchant audience URI bound into the mandate.

max_amount_minor.description: Spending cap in minor units, e.g. 10000 = 100.00 USD. Integers only.

name: drift_check
